title: Minimal Context Cross-Project Wakeup — Fast handoff between spokes
one_liner: Enable rapid context handoff when moving between projects: closeout specifies next project, wakeup loads minimal state + asks for details.
summary: Currently every wakeup loads full context (WAI-State.json, Skills, lug index, strategic context). When user switches projects (e.g., 'close wheelwright, start xyz'), next wakeup should skip 70% of that and ask 'which areas matter today?' to reconstruct focus.
motivation: Cross-project work is common. Full wakeup is ~46k tokens. Minimal wakeup could be ~8-12k. User controls depth with follow-up questions. Saves token budget for actual work.
acceptance_criteria: Closeout Step 9: Add `_next_session_context_preference` field to WAI-State.json with { project: string, minimal: boolean, focus_areas: string[] }
Wakeup Step 7: If minimal, load ONLY WAI-State.json (core identity), skip Skills/lug loads, present mini-briefing + 'Need more context? Ask for [lugs|skills|signals|strategic]'
Session tracks record context depth: 'minimal' vs 'full'
User can override with /wai-full to load complete context on-demand
scope: Modify wakeup Step 2 (state loading) to detect minimal flag
Modify wakeup Step 7 (briefing) to support minimal mode
Add /wai-full command to restore full context mid-session
Update closeout Step 9 (WAI-State updates) to set preference
implementation_notes: Minimal mode is opt-in at closeout ('next project: xyz, minimal mode'). Default is full wakeup. User always in control.
scope_verified_by: user feedback (Session 73: cross-project handoff feature for Wheelwright Framework)
routing_notes: Architectural improvement to Wheelwright's wakeup. Stays local. Becomes a teaching only if other spokes adopt similar pattern.
resolution_note: Implemented: Session 102 added Minimal Mode (--minimal flag, ~8k tokens), lazy-load skills (Step 3), lazy-load lugs (Step 4 counts only).
completion_note: Implemented: Session 102 added Minimal Mode (--minimal flag, ~8k tokens), lazy-load skills (Step 3), lazy-load lugs (Step 4 counts only).
